# 1. Introduction

This report examines alternative factor structures for trust in science and scientists using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and structural equation modeling (SEM).

The following models are examined:

1. Unidimensional CFA model
2. Simple-structure two-factor CFA model
3. Second-order CFA model
4. Bifactor CFA model
5. Bifactor SEM predicting belief in information
6. Bifactor SEM predicting trust in individual scientists

# 2. Data preparation

## 2.1. Load packages

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(lavaan)
library(qgraph)
library(semPlot)
library(haven)
library(semTools)
library(readxl)
```

## 2.2. Import the dataset

```{r import-data}
Data_Trust <- read_excel("TSModeling_Dataset.xlsx")

# Inspect the dataset
dim(Data_Trust)
names(Data_Trust)
head(Data_Trust)
```

## 2.3. Reverse-code items
The following items are reverse-coded using the transformation `6 - x`, assuming a five-point response scale ranging from 1 to 5.

```{r reverse-coding}
reverse_cols <- c(
  "ts1", "ts2", "ts3", "ts4", "ts6", "ts8",
  "ts13", "ts17", "ts18", "ts19", "ts20", "ts21"
)

Data_Trust[, reverse_cols] <-
  6 - Data_Trust[, reverse_cols]
```

# 3. Confirmatory factor analysis

## 3.1. Unidimensional CFA model

The unidimensional model specifies a single latent factor, `TrustinScienceScientist`, measured by all 21 observed items.

```{r cfa-unidimensional}
Model_Uni <- '
  TrustinScienceScientist =~
    ts1 + ts2 + ts3 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 +
    ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts12 + ts13 +
    ts14 + ts15 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 +
    ts20 + ts21
'

FitUni <- cfa(
  Model_Uni,
  data = Data_Trust,
  std.lv = TRUE
)

summary(
  FitUni,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

# Modification indices
modindices(FitUni)
```

## 3.2. Simple-structure two-factor CFA model

The two-factor model distinguishes between trust in science and trust in scientists.

- `TrustinScience` is measured by five items.
- `TrustinScientist` is measured by 16 items.

```{r cfa-simple-structure}
Model_Simple <- '
  TrustinScience =~
    ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21

  TrustinScientist =~
    ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 +
    ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 +
    ts18 + ts19 + ts20
'

FitSimple <- cfa(
  Model_Simple,
  data = Data_Trust
)

summary(
  FitSimple,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

# Modification indices
modindices(FitSimple)
```

## 3.3. Second-order CFA model

The second-order model specifies a general trust factor, `TrustGeneral`, underlying the two first-order factors.

```{r cfa-second-order}
Model_SecondOrder <- '
  TrustinScience =~
    ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21

  TrustinScientist =~
    ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 +
    ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 +
    ts18 + ts19 + ts20

  TrustGeneral =~
    TrustinScience + TrustinScientist
'

Fit_SecondOrder <- cfa(
  Model_SecondOrder,
  data = Data_Trust
)

summary(
  Fit_SecondOrder,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

# Modification indices
modindices(Fit_SecondOrder)
```

### 3.3.1. Constrained second-order model

The unconstrained second-order model may encounter identification problems or negative latent residual variances. The following version fixes the variance of the higher-order factor to 1 and fixes both first-order latent residual variances to 0.05.

```{r cfa-second-order-constrained}
Model_SecondOrder_Constrained <- '
  TrustinScience =~
    ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21

  TrustinScientist =~
    ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 +
    ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 +
    ts18 + ts19 + ts20

  TrustGeneral =~
    TrustinScience + TrustinScientist

  # Fix the variance of the higher-order factor
  TrustGeneral ~~ 1*TrustGeneral

  # Fix first-order latent residual variances
  TrustinScience ~~ 0.05*TrustinScience
  TrustinScientist ~~ 0.05*TrustinScientist
'

Fit_SecondOrder_Constrained <- cfa(
  Model_SecondOrder_Constrained,
  data = Data_Trust
)

summary(
  Fit_SecondOrder_Constrained,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

# Modification indices
modindices(Fit_SecondOrder_Constrained)
```

## 3.4. Bifactor CFA model

The bifactor model specifies a general trust factor loading on all 21 items and two specific factors representing trust in science and trust in scientists.

The general factor and the two specific factors are constrained to be mutually orthogonal.

```{r cfa-bifactor}
Model_Bi <- '
  # General factor
  TrustinScienceScientist =~
    ts1 + ts2 + ts3 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 +
    ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts12 + ts13 +
    ts14 + ts15 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 +
    ts20 + ts21

  # Specific factor: trust in science
  TrustinScience =~
    ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21

  # Specific factor: trust in scientists
  TrustinScientist =~
    ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 +
    ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 +
    ts18 + ts19 + ts20

  # Orthogonality constraints
  TrustinScienceScientist ~~ 0*TrustinScience
  TrustinScienceScientist ~~ 0*TrustinScientist
  TrustinScience ~~ 0*TrustinScientist
'

FitBi <- cfa(
  Model_Bi,
  data = Data_Trust
)

summary(
  FitBi,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

# Modification indices
modindices(FitBi)
```

# 4. Structural equation modeling

## 4.1. Bifactor SEM predicting belief in information

This model examines whether the general trust factor and the two specific trust factors predict `Outcome_beliefinfo`.

```{r sem-bifactor-belief-information}
Model_Bi1 <- '
  # General factor
  TrustinScienceScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts3 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 +
    ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts12 + ts13 + ts14 + ts15 + ts16 +
    ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20 + ts21

  # Specific factors
  TrustinScience =~ ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21
  TrustinScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 +
    ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20

  # Orthogonal bifactor structure
  TrustinScienceScientist ~~ 0*TrustinScience
  TrustinScienceScientist ~~ 0*TrustinScientist
  TrustinScience ~~ 0*TrustinScientist

  # Structural path to outcome
  Outcome_beliefinfo ~ TrustinScience + TrustinScientist + TrustinScienceScientist
'

SEMBi1 <- sem(
  Model_Bi1,
  data = Data_Trust,
  std.lv = TRUE
)

summary(
  SEMBi1,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)
```

## 4.2. Bifactor SEM predicting trust in individual scientists

This model examines whether the general trust factor and the two specific trust factors predict `Outcome_highcred`.

```{r sem-bifactor-individual-scientists}
Model_Bi2 <- '
  # General factor
  TrustinScienceScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts3 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 +
    ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts12 + ts13 + ts14 + ts15 + ts16 +
    ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20 + ts21

  # Specific factors
  TrustinScience =~ ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21
  TrustinScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 +
    ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20

  # Orthogonal bifactor structure
  TrustinScienceScientist ~~ 0*TrustinScience
  TrustinScienceScientist ~~ 0*TrustinScientist
  TrustinScience ~~ 0*TrustinScientist

  # Structural path to outcome
  Outcome_highcred ~ TrustinScience + TrustinScientist + TrustinScienceScientist
'

SEMBi2 <- sem(
  Model_Bi2,
  data = Data_Trust,
  std.lv = TRUE
)

summary(
  SEMBi2,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)
```

# 5. Model comparison

The following code extracts commonly reported fit indices from the fitted CFA and SEM models.

```{r model-comparison}
models <- list(
  Unidimensional = FitUni,
  SimpleStructure = FitSimple,
  SecondOrder = Fit_SecondOrder,
  SecondOrder_Constrained = Fit_SecondOrder_Constrained,
  Bifactor = FitBi,
  SEM_BeliefInformation = SEMBi1,
  SEM_IndividualScientists = SEMBi2
)

fit_indices <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(models), function(model_name) {
    fit <- fitMeasures(
      models[[model_name]],
      c(
        "chisq", "df", "pvalue",
        "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr",
        "aic", "bic"
      )
    )

    data.frame(
      Model = model_name,
      t(fit),
      row.names = NULL,
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  })
)

rownames(fit_indices) <- NULL

knitr::kable(
  fit_indices,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Fit indices for the CFA and SEM models"
)
```

# 6. Conclusion

This analysis compares alternative representations of trust in science and scientists and examines the predictive relationships between latent trust factors and the two outcomes.

Model selection should consider overall fit, parameter estimates, identification, residual variances, theoretical coherence, and the interpretability of the latent factors rather than relying exclusively on individual fit indices.
